You are checking a claim someone has made about a statutory provision. Your job is to REFUTE it if it can be refuted. Default to unsound when uncertain.

The claim asserts that, according to this provision, one quantity bears on another. The two most common ways such a claim is wrong:
  (a) SUBJECT MISMATCH. The provision governs something other than the quantity the claim says it determines. A provision about an insurer's duty to pay for treatment does not govern how much treatment occurred. A provision conferring jurisdiction to assess a claim does not make one assessed quantity a determinant of another.
  (b) WORD MATCHING. The claim latched onto a word rather than a meaning -- reading 'caused by the fault of the driver' (a fault condition) as being about how difficult causation is to establish.

A claim is sound only if the provision genuinely makes the first quantity bear on the second. Mentioning both is not enough. A precondition for the provision to operate is not automatically a determinant of its subject.

PROVISION: 84A Motor Accidents Compensation Act 1999

--- BEGIN PROVISION TEXT ---
84A
 
Duty of insurer to make interim payments in case of financial hardship
(1)
 Once liability has been admitted (wholly or in part) or determined (wholly or in part) against the person against whom the claim is made, it is the duty of an insurer to make payments to or on behalf of the claimant in respect of economic loss but only to the extent that such a payment is necessary to avoid the claimant suffering financial hardship.
Note.
A dispute about payments under this section may be referred to the Commission under section 96 for assessment.
(2)
 It is a condition of an insurer’s licence under Part 7.1 that the insurer must comply with this section.
(3)
 A payment made under this section to or on behalf of a claimant before the claimant obtains judgment for damages against the defendant is, to the extent of its amount, a defence to proceedings by the claimant against the defendant for damages.
(4)
 The amount of a payment made under this section to or on behalf of a claimant is to be included in the damages recoverable by the claimant for the purposes of any reduction of those damages by reason of the contributory negligence of the deceased or injured person.
Note.
If damages are to be reduced by reason of contributory negligence, subsection (4) ensures that the reduction extends to amounts paid by an insurer under this section.
s 84A:
 Ins 2007 No 95, Sch 1 [50]. Am 2020 No 18, Sch 6.7[28].
--- END PROVISION TEXT ---

THE CLAIM: this provision makes 'Liability Clarity' (an ordinal score for how clear fault is) bear on 'Future Economic Loss' (dollars awarded for future loss of earning capacity), as a gate.
Quoted in support: "Once liability has been admitted (wholly or in part) or determined (wholly or in part)"
Mapping offered: The clarity of liability affects whether the insurer must make interim payments, as the provision requires liability to be admitted or determined.

Refute this claim if it can be refuted.

response.objection: The provision is about the insurer's duty to make interim payments to avoid financial hardship, not about determining future economic loss awards. Liability clarity is a precondition for interim payments, not a determinant of future economic loss.
